name: Comgrow Z1 10W
tagline: 10W Budget Comgrow diode: often bundled with 3D printer deals
tldr: Comgrow Z1 10W is the 10W SKU on the Comgrow comgrow z1 line. Comgrow's Z1 targets entry-level buyers, often sold alongside Ender 3D printers. Verify optical power on the listing: do not assume combined-watt marketing.
mainObjective: High-quality hobby and light-business engraving with light, slow cutting

priceRange.note: 10W optical module: verify SKU before buying

engraveExample.description: Filled photo or logo on birch plywood

cutExample.description: Simple square cut-out from 3 mm basswood

pros: About a third faster than the 5W in our benchmark: ~18–28 min for a 10 × 10 cm photo, ~9–15 min for a 3 mm basswood square
The highest power listed in Comgrow's own Z1 manual (1.6W, 5W and 10W options)
cons: Still slow on cutting: 2–3 mm/s on 3 mm wood in our tests, so multi-pass beyond 3 mm
Slightly wider spot than the 5W (~0.09 mm vs ~0.08 mm), so photos are a touch softer
Comgrow publishes no per-thickness cutting chart: you will need your own test grids
beginnerNotes: This profile is the 10W SKU on Comgrow Z1. Read the TL;DR and benchmarks above, then compare other power options via the chips before buying.
proTips: Run material test grids at engraving speeds first. Add air assist for light cuts. If cut jobs exceed ~30% of your week, open the higher-watt profile on this site and compare times.

editorialDepth.advantages: Z1 10W fits casual engravers who want faster fills than 5W on a tight Comgrow deal.
editorialDepth.limitations: Businesses quoting cut-outs should buy 20W tier. Compare Sculpfun S9 on sale before committing.

faq.question: How thick can the Comgrow Z1 10W cut?
faq.answer: Comgrow gives no official thickness per pass. Our profile lists thin basswood with multiple passes, plus paper, card and fabric; our 3 mm basswood test square takes ~9–15 min at 2–3 mm/s. Treat 3 mm as the comfortable limit and test anything thicker on scrap first.

faq.question: Is the Z1 10W good for photo engraving?
faq.answer: Yes for gifts and small batches. Our benchmark puts a 10 × 10 cm filled photo at ~18–28 min, against ~28–43 min on the 5W, with fill speeds of 9–21 mm/s. Lower the speed rather than raising power on light woods to avoid scorching.

faq.question: Z1 10W or Z1 20W: which one fits a small side business?
faq.answer: If you mostly engrave and cut only card or 3 mm wood, the 10W ($219–299) is the better value. If cut pieces are part of your orders, the 20W listing ($279–379) cuts our 3 mm test square in ~6–10 min and reaches 8 mm basswood; check its optical rating first, since Comgrow's own Z1 manual only lists modules up to 10W.

standoutFeatures.title: The balanced Z1
standoutFeatures.body: About a third shorter engraving and cutting times than the 5W in our benchmark, for roughly $40 more.

standoutFeatures.title: Top module in Comgrow's manual
standoutFeatures.body: Comgrow's Z1 manual lists 1.6W, 5W and 10W laser options: the 10W is the strongest one the brand documents itself.
